before.title: G6 2.4L Ecotec (LE5/LAT) Timing Chain Stretch
before.description: The 2.4L Ecotec LE5 in 2007-2010 G6 (and shared Cobalt SS, Malibu, HHR, Saturn Aura/Ion, Solstice) develops timing chain stretch — a very well-documented engineering issue across Ecotec forums and independent shops. Root cause: GM's original Oil Life Monitor allowed intervals up to 12,000 miles, starving the chain. Note: while GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment 11340C covering timing chain stretch on the 3.6L LFX/LLT V6, the 2.4L Ecotec did NOT receive the same blanket warranty extension. Some owners obtained goodwill repairs through dealer-level escalation.
before.solution: Full timing chain kit replacement (chain, tensioner, guides) ~$1,200-$2,000. If you experience the issue under 100,000 miles, request a goodwill-assistance review at a GM/Chevy dealer (not all approved, but some are). Use dexos1 full-synthetic 5W-30 and stick to 5,000-mile intervals going forward.

proposal.title: G6 2.4L Ecotec (LE5/LAT) Timing Chain Stretch
proposal.description: The frozen page assigns timing-chain stretch to every 2007-2010 2.4L LE5/LAT G6 and attributes it to long oil-life intervals. The complete 1,418-row exact G6 manufacturer-communications corpus instead identifies timing-chain conditions on high-feature V6 applications, including records 10020691, 10022931, 10052863 and the 10245793-10245795 series. Those records do not establish a 2.4L LE5/LAT population, an oil-starvation mechanism, a 12,000-mile interval or goodwill coverage.
proposal.solution: Confirm engine RPO, oil level and pressure, noise location, correlation codes and cam/crank timing data before opening the timing drive. Separate chain, tensioner, actuator, sensor, reluctor and lubrication paths under current service information. Do not buy a timing-chain kit, guides, tensioner, oil or actuator from this page; the indexed engine claim lacks exact support and the failed path, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: chain, actuator, sensor and reluctor paths separated

before.title: Front wheel bearing/hub failure (humming/grinding noise)
before.description: The sealed front wheel bearing/hub assemblies on the 2005-2010 G6 commonly wear out, producing a loud humming or grinding noise that rises with speed and changes when turning. If a turn to one side worsens the noise, the failing bearing is typically on the opposite side. Left unrepaired, a bearing can seize or fail completely, which is a serious safety risk.
before.solution: Replace the affected front wheel bearing/hub assembly (a bolt-on unit). They are often replaced in pairs; quality units (e.g., Timken/SKF) are recommended.
symptoms: Noise changes when turning left vs right

before.title: Intake manifold gasket coolant leak (3.5L V6)
before.description: The 3.5L 'wet' V6 routes engine coolant through passages in the intake manifold, and the original plastic-framed lower intake manifold gaskets degrade and leak. This causes external coolant loss or, worse, coolant leaking internally and mixing with the engine oil, which can damage bearings and lead to overheating. (The later 3.9L V6 uses a 'dry' intake and is not prone to the same failure.)
before.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets, ideally with an upgraded metal-framed set (e.g., Fel-Pro). It's a 4-6 hour job; check the oil for a milky appearance before driving as a contaminated engine should not be run.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Sweet smell / coolant near the manifold
Milky/foamy oil on dipstick or oil cap

before.title: Low-Beam Headlight Connector Melting / Pigtail Burn
before.description: The headlight low-beam (H11/9006) connector on 2005-2010 G6s develops corrosion and high resistance, generating heat that melts the socket and pigtail. Owners report low beams burning out every few months, fuses popping, and visible browned/charred connectors when the bulb is pulled. Affects both sides, but driver's side first.
before.solution: Replace the melted bulb socket pigtail with a ceramic high-temperature H11 connector kit (14-gauge wire) and pack the new connector with dielectric grease. Inspect both sides even if only one has failed.

before.title: Low-beam headlights repeatedly fail (melted bulb connector/socket)
before.description: The G6 is notorious for low-beam headlights that burn out or stop working repeatedly. The root cause is that the bulb generates more heat than the cheap plastic headlamp connector/socket can handle, so the connector overheats, melts, and loses contact. Owners often replace bulbs only to have them fail again within months because the connector and wiring are the real problem.
before.solution: Replace the melted bulb socket/connector pigtail (often sold as a repair harness). A durable fix is upgrading to ceramic or gold-plated soldered connectors. Inspect fuses (commonly 7 and 9) and the headlight switch/wiring for corrosion.
symptoms: One or both low beams stop working
High beams still work but low beams don't
Headlight bulbs burn out every few months

before.title: Panoramic sunroof leaks and mechanical failures
before.description: G6 sedans equipped with the large panoramic (multi-panel) sunroof commonly leak water into the cabin. The frequent culprit is the sunroof drain tubes, which GM cut short, allowing them to pull off their outlets so water drains onto the seat belts, under the rear seat, and into the carpet. Owners also report the motorized sunshade buckling/breaking, panel pins/screws falling out, and the roof getting stuck.
before.solution: Clear and re-secure or replace the sunroof drain tubes so they stay seated at the outlets; repair or replace the sunshade mechanism and any loose panel hardware. Keep drains clear of debris.
symptoms: Water in rear footwell / under rear seat

before.title: Panoramic Sunroof Water Leak from Disconnected Drain Tubes
before.description: On 2005-2007 G6 sedans equipped with the optional four-panel C3Y panoramic sunroof, the factory drain tubes at the rear of the sunroof tray were cut too short and pop off the body grommets, dumping water into the headliner, rear floor, and trunk. GM issued service bulletin 06-08-57-004E (revised March 2009) with longer drain extensions for both panoramic and regular sunroof variants but did not formally recall it. The panoramic option was discontinued after 2007; 2008-2010 G6s have a smaller single-panel sunroof that can also exhibit similar drain issues addressed by the same TSB.
before.solution: Reattach and extend rear sunroof drains per GM TSB 06-08-57-004E (use longer hose with proper grommets). Clear all four drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air. Avoid wire snakes, which can puncture the tubes.
symptoms: Wet headliner or rear floor carpet after rain
Water in trunk near rear seat back

before.title: Passlock anti-theft no-start (security light on)
before.description: The G6's Passlock theft-deterrent system can falsely trip, illuminating the security light and preventing the engine from starting. The common cause is a worn ignition lock cylinder/Passlock sensor that fails to read the lock rotation correctly. The well-known 10-minute relearn trick only resets it temporarily; the fault usually returns until the cylinder/sensor is replaced.
before.solution: Temporary: turn key to ON and wait ~10 minutes until the security light stops flashing (repeat the relearn cycle as needed). Permanent fix is replacing the ignition lock cylinder / Passlock sensor and relearning the system, sometimes with a fresh dealer key.

before.description: G6 owners frequently see a 'Reduced Engine Power' message with the car dropping into limp mode, triggered by throttle position sensor voltage-correlation faults. The throttle body's integrated TPS develops dirty or shorting solder points (sometimes attributed to 'tin whiskers') and corrosion at the connector, so the two throttle sensor signals disagree and the ECM cuts power for safety.
before.solution: Inspect and clean the throttle body and TPS connector; check wiring for corrosion/water intrusion. The common fix is replacing the electronic throttle body assembly; relearn the throttle after replacement.
symptoms: Sudden loss of acceleration / limp mode

before.title: Retractable Hardtop Hydraulic Pump and Microswitch Failures
before.description: The G6 convertible (2007-2009) uses a complex 2-piece clamshell retractable hardtop with hydraulic rams and multiple position sensors. before.title: Rocker Panel and Lower Door Rust-Through
before.description: G6 rocker panels and lower door edges develop severe rust-through, especially in salt-belt states. The rockers are welded into the body sill (not bolt-on), with poor factory undercoating in the seam. Owners report visible holes and crumbling metal by 8-12 years of age. Same pattern as sibling Saturn Aura and Chevy Malibu (Epsilon platform).
before.solution: Catch early: grind to bare metal, treat with rust converter, prime and topcoat. Advanced cases require cut-and-weld rocker patch panels ($200 per side in parts, ~$1000 body-shop labor). GM's 6-year/100k corrosion warranty has long expired on these vehicles.
symptoms: Rust holes ahead of rear wheel arch

before.title: StabiliTrak / Traction Control / ABS Warning from BCM Connector Corrosion
before.description: Common G6 fault pattern: simultaneous Service StabiliTrak, Service Traction Control, ABS warning lights, and sometimes Reduced Engine Power message. GM-acknowledged issue (TSB) traced to fretting corrosion on terminals of the Body Control Module connectors (especially the C2 connector) located behind the passenger kick panel. Micro-vibration causes oxidation on the contact surfaces; moisture intrusion from sunroof drains can accelerate it.
before.solution: Remove the passenger kick panel to access the three large BCM connectors (especially the C2 connector); unlatch via the plastic levers, inspect for green/fretting corrosion, clean with electrical contact cleaner, apply dielectric grease per GM procedure (one-inch nylon bristle brush on C2 pins), and re-seat several times. Note: the 'Reduced Engine Power' message specifically is often caused by a separate IP-to-body harness connector in the DRIVER-side (left) kick panel carrying the APP signal — inspect both sides. Do NOT replace the BCM for this condition. Also scan wheel-speed and steering-position sensors before condemning the BCM.
symptoms: Service StabiliTrak and Service Traction Control messages

before.title: Sudden loss of electric power steering (EPS) assist
before.description: The Pontiac G6's electric power steering can suddenly lose assist while driving, requiring much greater effort to steer, especially at low speeds. The failure traces to the torque sensor assembly and/or EPS motor controller and was the single most-complained-about defect on the G6. GM issued a federal recall (NHTSA 14V153000, expanded by 15V064000) covering 2005-2009 models.
before.solution: Under recall, dealers replace the torque sensor assembly and/or EPS motor controller unit per the bulletin matching the vehicle's build date, free of charge. Out of recall, the EPS column/motor or torque sensor is replaced. Many owners reported onset around 70,000-100,000 miles.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy/hard to turn
Loss of assist at low speed or when parking
Intermittent assist that comes and goes

proposal.title: Sudden loss of electric power steering (EPS) assist
proposal.description: NHTSA campaigns 14V153000 and 15V064000 together cover affected 2005-2009 Pontiac G6 vehicles for sudden loss of electric power-steering assist. The campaign-wide 1,373,177 figure is not a G6-only count, and exact sources do not support calling this the single most-complained-about defect or assigning a 70,000-100,000-mile onset.
proposal.solution: A sudden loss of assist requires greater steering effort, especially at low speed; reduce speed and stop safely if control is affected. Check the VIN with NHTSA and GM for open campaigns and have codes/build applicability diagnosed before repair. Ask the dealer to confirm current remedy availability and any charge in 2026. Do not buy a torque sensor, column, EPS motor or controller from this page; the applicable bulletin, failed component, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

before.title: Transmission shift cable / vehicle not actually in Park (rollaway)
before.description: On G6 models with the 4-speed automatic, the tabs on the transmission shift cable end can fracture/separate, or the shift cable adjustment clip may not be fully engaged. When this happens the shifter position and the actual transmission gear no longer match, so the driver can move the lever to Park and remove the key while the transmission is not truly in Park. This created a documented rollaway hazard and was the subject of NHTSA recalls 09V073000 and 14V224000.
before.solution: Under recall, dealers install a retainer/clip over the cable end or replace the shift cable as necessary, at no charge. Out of recall, the shift cable assembly is replaced. Use the parking brake until repaired.
symptoms: Shifter says Park but car can roll
Key can be removed while not fully in Park
Vehicle rolls away after being parked
Shift lever position doesn't match gear
Hard to get out of or into Park
